review_scope.mode: independent hostile validation, no tools, all artifacts treated as untrusted data
review_scope.candidate: fresh immutable round-12 candidate as supplied inline (design, catalog contracts/schemas/API, bridge-config.sql, tooling, 36 test modules, receipts, release-010 reconciliation set, scale checkpoint, owner audits, ledger)
review_scope.phase: implementable Android MCP bridge design plus executable catalog/extractor/schema/API and offline reference contracts; Android app/HTTP/MCP hosting, device probes, deployment, commits, pushes not requested
review_scope.not_executed_by_reviewer: tests, hashes, builds, browsing; all such values are supplied claims checked only for internal consistency

design.rationale: Startup/device-resolution sections, authority separation, traceability and Mermaid provenance (R11-10) are correct and current. Accuracy deductions: capacity section still reasons from release-008 size/hash while production is 010; the design asserts 'inherited oneway' semantics the extractor does not produce (R12-02); FR-DEV-02 evidence axes are described as inputs although no producer exists (R12-03). Completeness deduction: no stated disposition for the unmet memory budget and the unimplemented native SQLite resolution path.

contracts_schema.rationale: DeviceResolution 2.1.0, DeviceView 3.0.0, openapi 1.4.0, dv2 6-field ETag and bridge-config.sql pins/guards verified against each other and against the oracles. Deductions: API-CONTRACT.md documents two incompatible dv2 ETag shapes (R12-04); SQL document-pin trigger admits JSON null (R12-08); 2.1.0 schema still carries a 2.0.0 Snapshot/Header definition that only prose marks historical (R12-13).

extractor.rationale: R11-02/03/04/05/07/08/09/12/13 and P11-01..06 verified in code with fixtures. Accuracy deduction: interface-level oneway is never written into extras, so format-3 contract digests of methods on 'oneway interface' declarations are wrong in builder output and only a synthetic dict is tested (R12-02); null schema_hash aliases are emitted (R12-11). Completeness deductions: no extractor produces interface/modules/oem/build_fingerprints clauses, leaving all AIDL/HIDL variants unknown by construction (R12-03); 010 build shows 1268 retained-unsupported sources and 8 unsupported manifests (R12-07); two test modules present in the 010 snapshot are absent from the candidate without a recorded reason (R12-09); performance evidence exists only for superseded code (R12-10).

production_catalog_data.rationale: Release 010 counts reconcile internally (entry kinds sum 802936, source kinds 44397, declarations 1125985, annotation buckets 13334, permission names 719, AIDL statuses 20210) and inventory/registry digests are reported byte-equivalent. Accuracy is capped because 010 was built by pre-candidate code and embodies semantics the candidate has since corrected: fabricated platform point intervals (R11-02), format-2 digests over raw headers (R11-05), AIDL/HIDL fields classified as bindings (R11-09), no interface oneway (R12-02); provenance states production_equals_latest_candidate:false and the candidate loader rejects a non-2.1.0 inventory (R12-01). Completeness: 846 unmatched annotations and 2 undefined permission names persist; HIDL (962 files) and the annotation owner fallback are not in production; 732 of 985 outside projects remain unknown with 27696 uninspected filename candidates; 1268 retained-unsupported sources; no interface/module evidence for any AIDL binding. Acknowledgement does not substitute for coverage.

overall.method: Not an average. Overall completeness is bounded by the required all-public binding/permission coverage, which the production catalog does not yet reach; overall accuracy reflects that every verified category defect is either disclosed or small except R12-01/R12-02.
overall.distance_to_98_98: Requires an immutable production rebuild from the frozen candidate (R12-01), the oneway builder fix (R12-02), a real producer for interface/module evidence (R12-03), disclosure and reduction of retained-unsupported sources (R12-07), and measurable closure of the outside-corpus and annotation residuals (R12-15, R12-16).

findings.evidence: provenance: "production_equals_latest_candidate": false, "ddl_matches_candidate": false; 17 differing files incl. DeviceView.schema.json, effective_device_inventory.py, hidl_source.py listed absent in production; candidate build_catalog writes manifest urn:android-binding-catalog:2.1.0:DeviceResolution while production DeviceResolution.schema sha256 is baa447f5… (2.0); candidate load_inventory requires catalog_meta device_resolution_contract_version=='2.1.0'.
findings.issue: The only production catalog (010) is not an output of the validated candidate tooling. All semantic corrections verified in this round (point semantics, format-3 digests, entity kinds, java.lang fallback, overlays, DeviceView 3 pins) are absent from the data that is scored as production, and the candidate oracle cannot load the production inventory without a rebuild.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Freeze the candidate hashes, rebuild an immutable release 011 from them, publish provenance with production_equals_latest_candidate:true and ddl_matches_candidate:true, and regenerate device-inventory/export/production reconciliation receipts against 011.
findings.verification_needed: Rebuild receipts and reconciliation artifacts for 011; not executable in this no-tools review.

findings.artifact: catalog/tooling/build_catalog.py (AIDL member loop); catalog/tooling/parsers.py (member, aidl); catalog/tooling/dispatch_manifest.py (contract_digest); catalog/tests/test_round11.py
findings.evidence: build_catalog member loop assigns r['extras']['imports']=d['imports'], r['extras']['interface_annotations'], r['extras']['interface_permission'] and never assigns interface_oneway; parsers.member sets oneway=bool(re.search(r'\boneway\b',body[:a])) over the method text only; parsers.aidl sets declaration-level oneway=kind=='interface' and …; contract_digest reads extras interface_oneway; the only interface-oneway test passes the synthetic dict {'oneway':False,'interface_oneway':False}.
findings.issue: For 'oneway interface IFoo { void bar(); }' every method is digested with oneway=false in builder output. contract_hash, schema_hash and policy identity are therefore wrong for inherited-oneway methods, and the design/README statement 'inherited oneway' is not implemented. The fixture never exercises the builder, so the regression suite cannot detect it.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: In the build_catalog member loop add r['extras']['interface_oneway']=bool(d.get('oneway')); add a builder-level fixture that parses an 'oneway interface' source and asserts contract_digest(…)['oneway'] is true and differs from the non-oneway digest.
findings.verification_needed: New fixture run plus a rebuilt contract-hash sample for one oneway interface.

findings.evidence: lifecycle_rule emits only index ranges/extension alternatives, dict(alternatives=[dict(platform_point=point)],evidence_ids=evidence), or unknown_reason 'Source API major alone does not prove minor applicability'; no code path constructs clauses keyed interface, modules, oem or build_fingerprints; scale states_by_source_kind: aidl 0 available/52427 unknown, sdk-signature 0/97830, source-signature 0/141515.
findings.issue: The startup requirement (FR-DEV-02/TR-DEV-02) demands resolution from SDK extensions, OEM/build/module versions and interface version/hash/reachability. Those evidence axes exist only in the 2.1.0 schema and hand-written fixtures. Stable-AIDL aidl_api/<iface>/<N>/.hash files and Mainline module metadata are never imported, so no AIDL or HIDL binding can ever resolve to available.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Add an extractor that reads stable-AIDL aidl_api/*/{N,current}/.hash into interface clauses (version, hash) and APEX/module manifests into modules clauses; until then emit unknown_reason naming the missing evidence class and state in the design that AIDL/HIDL availability is unknown by construction.
findings.verification_needed: Builder fixture with an aidl_api hash file and a non-zero aidl available count in a scale receipt.

findings.evidence: Contains "dv2:<scope_sha256>:<view_generation>:<capability_epoch>:<catalog_generation>:<overlay_generation>" in the 'additive contract 1.3' section and later "dv2:…:<overlay_generation>:<inventory_sha256>"; device_resolution.etag() and openapi.json pattern use six fields.
findings.issue: Two incompatible ETag definitions in one contract version; a client implementing the first form will fail If-Match preconditions.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Mark the five-field form as '1.3, superseded' or delete it, and add a test asserting the documented regex matches device_resolution.etag() output.
findings.verification_needed: Doc diff and one regex test.

findings.evidence: Trigger condition json_type(new.document_json,'$.catalog_document_sha256') IS NOT NULL accepts a JSON null value (json_type returns 'null'); pipeline test publishes rows from raw load_inventory into DeviceViewStore and seals successfully without effective pins.
findings.issue: A sealed, active view can hold available entries with no catalog document pin; only alias generation and the policy gate later deny them, so the storage invariant 'every available member pins its document' is not enforced where it is declared.
findings.exact_minimal_correction: Change the predicate to json_type(...)='text' and require a 64-char hex value; in publish, reject available entries lacking catalog_document_sha256 when the inventory is effective; make the pipeline test assert rejection or a non-dispatchable seal.

limitations: No tools: no test execution, hash recomputation, SQL execution or file retrieval; every receipt value is a submitter claim checked only for internal arithmetic consistency.

Not reviewed: the 010 catalog.sqlite itself, the full 19.3 MB native validation report, per-source rows, the 27696 filename candidate list, full HIDL record set, and the 43 MB api-lifecycle-facts.jsonl.
Public Android platform claims (SDK extension semantics, stable-AIDL hash layout, Binder flags) rely on cited references and prior knowledge, not fresh browsing.
Owner HIDL and annotation-fallback results are owner audits on fixtures, not production outputs, and were scored as such.
Scale checkpoint code hashes differ from the candidate; its numbers describe superseded code.
Evidence quotations are reproduced from the supplied inline artifacts as read; line numbers are not asserted.
